How it works

Three steps between you and less repetition.

CommonCopy stays quietly in the Windows notification area until you need it.

1

Highlight or write

Save text you select in another app, or create a phrase directly in the manager.

2

Open CommonCopy

Press Ctrl + Shift + Space or Ctrl + Right Click from almost any application.

3

Choose and continue

Select a phrase and CommonCopy pastes it into the field you were already using.

Built for daily work

Simple enough to disappear. Useful enough to keep.

Privacy by design

Your phrases stay on your computer.

CommonCopy is local-first software. It does not need an account, an Internet connection, or a cloud service to do its job.

Read the privacy details
  • No phrase uploads or cloud synchronization
  • No keystroke logging or recording what you type
  • No desktop advertising or application analytics
  • Human-readable local storage and backups

FAQ

Useful answers before you install.

Does CommonCopy work in every Windows application?

It is designed to paste into standard text fields across Windows. Some elevated, protected, remote, or unusually implemented applications may restrict simulated paste input and require additional compatibility work.

Does it replace the normal right-click menu?

No. Your normal right-click remains unchanged. CommonCopy appears only when you use its configured Ctrl + Right Click gesture, or its keyboard shortcut.

Can it save text I highlight in another app?

Yes. Highlight selectable text, open CommonCopy, and choose Save highlighted text…. You can review the generated title and category before saving. Copy-protected or image-only content may not be available.

Where are my phrases stored?

CommonCopy stores them as local JSON under your Windows user profile. The manager also provides import, export, backup, and restore tools.

Can I store passwords in CommonCopy?

No. The initial version stores phrases as readable local text. Use a dedicated password manager for passwords, authentication codes, and recovery keys.

Is CommonCopy really open source?

Yes. The application is MIT licensed. The source is available at GitHub.

Free software, built in the open.

CommonCopy’s desktop application remains free and open source. Browse the source, report issues, and contribute through the public repository.
